absent: Concrete values of encryption modes, key types and maximum key size; only containers and flags shown.
Implementations of inner encryption submit, crypt clone, integrity action decider and queue stacking; only call sites shown.
Concurrency and calling context rules for bio, request and integrity objects beyond hardware context dispatch locks.
DMA mapping iteration protocol and error handling beyond coalesce query and unmap completion.
Flush, scheduler, timeout and tag allocation behaviours referenced by request and hardware context fields.

findings.text: Encryption configuration carries a mode identifier, a data unit size, a length in bytes for the data unit number, a key type identifier, and integer flags. It is embedded in larger key state and guides submission decisions.

Software secret length is thirty two bytes, hardware allow flag is bit zero, maximum initialization vector length is thirty two bytes, and data unit number array length is the vector maximum divided by eight byte units.

Key object bundles the encryption configuration with a logarithmic form of data unit size, a size field, and a byte array sized by the largest supported key length. It is referenced read only from bio context.
Per bio encryption context holds a constant pointer to the key object and a fixed array of sixty four bit data unit number words whose length follows the vector maximum.

Presence and accessor helpers have two builds. When encryption support is present they expose the bio stored context pointer and test for non null. When absent they constantly report no context and null. Callers must handle both.

Submission wrapper for possibly encrypted bios first checks for a crypt context and tries an encryption aware submit path. If either there is no context or that path requests fallback, it uses the normal bio submission path.

Clone helper propagates encryption state from source to destination only when the source carries a context, delegating to an inner clone routine in that case and otherwise reporting success without action.
Three headers use conventional include guards to ensure single inclusion. Their guard macros have no behavioural effect beyond preventing repeated definition.
Integrity flag enumeration defines six single bit values from bit zero through bit five for no verify, no generate, device capable, reference tag, stacked, and split interval capable.
Stacking helper for a block device forwards to generic queue limits stacking by supplying the limits of the queue belonging to the partition disk.

Integrity support queries differ by build. Enabled build treats nonzero metadata size as support and returns the queue integrity object or null when unsupported, with device level helpers resolving through the disk. Disabled build always reports no support and null.
Maximum integrity segment query returns the configured queue limit when integrity is enabled and zero when disabled.

Enabled helpers derive protection interval count from sector count by shifting according to interval exponent relative to sector size, and byte count by scaling intervals with metadata size. Disabled builds constantly return zero.
Request integrity test checks the integrity command flag in the enabled build and constantly reports false in the disabled build.
Integrity vector accessor in the enabled build builds a vector from the bio integrity vector array and iterator state, while the disabled build returns an empty vector expected to be optimized away.
Bio vector iterator helpers select an array entry by index, then derive page, length bounded by remaining size, offset advanced by iterator offset, and a composed vector from those three parts.

When integrity or related mapping support is unavailable, metadata capability reports not supported, segment counting and mapping report zero, user mapping reports invalid argument, DMA iterator start and next report no progress, and device integrity lookup returns null.
Integrity action enumeration defines three single bit actions for buffer allocation, check or generate, and zeroing, using bits zero through two.
Integrity action selector returns no action when the bio device has no integrity support or the bio already carries integrity, otherwise it delegates to an inner action decider.

DMA mapping iteration state pairs a bio vector iterator with bio pointer, vector array and integrity marker, extended by address and length outputs, peer to peer state, completion status valid on failure, and embedded mapping iterator for internal progress.
Coalescing query reports whether the address translation state indicates use of virtualized addresses.

Unmap helper treats bus address mappings as needing no work, tears down virtualized address mappings with host bridge attributes when relevant and reports completion, otherwise reports the negation of whether the device still needs unmapping.

Direction and operation helpers classify a request as write or read and select device bound or host bound transfer direction accordingly. Passthrough detection masks to the operation field and matches driver input or output operations. Priority lookup uses the first bio priority or zero when no bio is attached.
Default queue depths are four minimum and one hundred twenty eight normal. Completion disposition has two values for no action and for freeing.
Request flag word is a thirty two bit bitwise distinct integer type used for strongly checked flag combinations.

Request behavior flags enumerate sequential bit positions from started through reserved, each exposed as a single bit mask in the flag word type. A combined no merge mask unions started, flush sequence and special payload.
Multiqueue request lifetime has three ordered states for idle, in flight and complete with numeric values zero through two.
Error handling timer outcome has two alternatives for finished and for rearming the timer.

Request descriptor links queue, software and hardware contexts, operation and behavior flags, tag identities, timeout and length plus sector cursor, bio chain, partition, timing stamps, statistics and segment counts, gap hint, optional encryption context and slot, lifecycle state with reference count and deadline, scheduler hash or completion list linkage, scheduler tree node or special payload vector, scheduler private area, flush sequence state, fifo time and completion callback with data.
Physical gap mask helper derives an address alignment mask from the stored gap bit position, clearing low bits below the gap granularity.

Singly linked request list helpers test emptiness, initialize head and tail, append or prepend, remove and return the head, peek at the head, and iterate with plain and safe forms that follow next links.

Safe iteration form reads the next link before testing the current node, so applying it to an empty list dereferences a null head while capturing next. Callers must only use it on non empty lists or guard emptiness first.

Hardware queue context groups a cache aligned dispatch section with lock, pending list and state flags, delayed run work, cpu affinity and round robin selectors, behaviour flags, scheduler and queue and flush queue links, driver data, software queue bitmap and dispatch source with load estimate, type and software queue array, dispatch wait lock with wait entry and index, driver and scheduler tag sets, numa and queue numbers, active count, cpu hotplug nodes, kernel object, optional debug directories and an idle list node.
Dispatch list and its state are guarded by the queue lock in the aligned section, while the dispatch wait queue and its insertion index are guarded by a separate dispatch wait lock.
Queue mapping holds a cpu to queue table pointer together with queue count and starting offset.
Hardware context types enumerate default, read and poll followed by a count sentinel, giving three usable types.

Tag set descriptor carries operation callbacks, per type queue maps with map count, hardware queue count and depth plus reserved count, command extension size, numa policy, timeout and flags, driver data, per queue tag tables with optional shared tags, list lock and tag list, sleepable update contexts, and a semaphore serializing hardware queue count changes.
Dispatch outcome pairs a request pointer with a last item marker. A companion iterator callback visits a request with opaque data and reports whether to continue.

Inline block layer interfaces for encryption submission and cloning, integrity queries, vector iteration, multiqueue list handling and DMA mapping are provided header local for direct caller use without separate linkage.
